── typescript/units.ts
// Code generated by ritsu <version>. DO NOT EDIT.
// The types of the units the package's rules and books take amounts in, one type of each unit (ritsu gen). The modules of the rules and the clients of the books name these types, so that the type checker keeps an amount of one unit from where another unit is taken.

export type GBPc = bigint & { readonly __rulec: "GBPc" }; // money[GBPc]
export type Gram = bigint & { readonly __rulec: "Gram" }; // mass[g]

── python/acme_pricing/units.py
# Code generated by ritsu <version>. DO NOT EDIT.
"""The types of the units the package's rules and books take amounts in, one type of each unit (ritsu gen). The modules of the rules and the clients of the books name these types, so that the type checker keeps an amount of one unit from where another unit is taken."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import NewType

GBPc = NewType("GBPc", int)  # money[GBPc]
Gram = NewType("Gram", int)  # mass[g]

── go/units/units.go
// Code generated by ritsu <version>. DO NOT EDIT.

// Package units is the types of the units the package's rules and books take amounts in, one type of each
// unit (ritsu gen). The packages of the rules and the clients of the books name these types, so that the
// compiler keeps an amount of one unit from where another unit is taken.
package units

// GBPc is an amount of money[GBPc].
type GBPc int64

// Gram is an amount of mass[g].
type Gram int64
